title: Minimum Weighted Subgraph With the Required Paths
summary: Given an integer n for the number of nodes in a weighted directed graph, and a 2D array of edges with their weights, along with three distinct node numbers src1, src2, and dest, find the minimum weight of a subgraph allowing travel from both src1 and src2 to dest.
statement: Given an integer n for the number of nodes in a weighted directed graph, and a 2D array of edges with their weights, along with three distinct node numbers src1, src2, and dest, find the minimum weight of a subgraph allowing travel from both src1 and src2 to dest. If no such subgraph exists, return -1. A subgraph consists of a subset of the original graph's nodes and edges.
constraints: The directed graph has nonnegative edge weights and may contain parallel edges.
Choose a subgraph containing paths from both sources to dest; shared suffix edges are paid only once.
Return its minimum total weight, or -1 when no valid subgraph exists.
hints: Any optimal pair of paths can be viewed as two prefixes meeting at a node followed by one shared suffix.
Compute distances from each source and distances to dest by running Dijkstra from dest on reversed edges.
Minimize dist1[v]+dist2[v]+to_dest[v] over every possible meeting node.
The formula constructs a valid union for every meeting node, while the first common node of any optimal paths yields a candidate no heavier than that union.
